Find splice events from annotated exons

Source: R/find_events.R
find_events.Rd

Functions to find different types of alternative splicing events from preprocessed GRanges exon data. Events include skipped exon (se), included exon (ie), consecutive skipped exons (cse), consecutive included exons (cie), mutatualy exclusive exons (mxe), retained intron (ri), spliced intron (si), alternative 5' and 3' splice sites (a5ss / a3ss), and alternative transcription start and end sites (atss / ates).

find_ie(), find_cie() and find_si() are the reverse of find_se(), find_cse() and find_ri(): the same comparison with the up and down transcripts swapped. A spliced intron is an intron of an up transcript that a down transcript retains, i.e. an intron that the up transcript splices out.

find_se() reports an exon skipped on its own: both of its neighbours are kept by the partner transcript. Two or more consecutive exons skipped together are reported by find_cse() instead, one row per exon, when the exons on either side of the run match rank-adjacent exons of the partner and no exon of the run overlaps the partner. The exons of one run are the consecutive exon_rank values within a tx_id / event_tx_id pair. A run that reaches the first or last exon is not a cse; find_atss() / find_ates() cover it.

find_a5ss() / find_a3ss() do not require either boundary of an exon to be shared with its partner, so an exon that moved both boundaries is reported as an a5ss and an a3ss. A first exon has no acceptor and a last exon has no donor, so those boundaries never produce an a3ss / a5ss, whether the first or last exon belongs to the up or to the down transcript of the pair; find_atss() / find_ates() report them instead by comparing where each transcript begins and ends. The other boundary of a first or last exon is a real splice site and is still compared. exon_rank runs in transcription order, so this holds on both strands.

When an exon overlaps two or more exons of its partner (a retained or spliced intron), the boundaries facing the intron are left to find_ri() / find_si(); only the outer boundaries of the group are compared. An exon that retains an intron and uses a different outer splice site is therefore reported as both an ri (or si) and an a5ss / a3ss.

Usage

find_se(gr, type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"), inverse = FALSE, ...)

find_skipped_exons(
  gr,
  type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"),
  inverse = FALSE,
  ...
)

find_ie(gr, type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"), ...)

find_included_exons(gr, type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"), ...)

find_cse(gr, type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"), inverse = FALSE, ...)

find_consecutive_skipped_exons(
  gr,
  type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"),
  inverse = FALSE,
  ...
)

find_cie(gr, type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"), ...)

find_consecutive_included_exons(
  gr,
  type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"),
  ...
)

find_mxe(gr, type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"), ...)

find_mutually_exclusive_exons(
  gr,
  type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"),
  ...
)

find_ri(gr, inverse = FALSE)

find_retained_introns(gr, inverse = FALSE)

find_si(gr)

find_spliced_introns(gr)

find_a5ss(gr)

find_alternative_5_prime_splice_sites(gr)

find_a3ss(gr)

find_alternative_3_prime_splice_sites(gr)

find_atss(gr)

find_alternative_transcription_start_sites(gr)

find_ates(gr)

find_alternative_transcription_end_sites(gr)

find_all_events(
  gr,
  type = c("over", "boundary", "identical"),
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

gr

A GRanges object with exon annotations, including 'tx_id', 'exon', and 'coef_col' metadata columns and preprocessed with preprocess().

type

How an exon flanking a candidate is matched to an exon of the partner transcript. One of:

"over"

(default) any overlap, with no coordinate in common required. The most permissive setting.

"boundary"

the two exons overlap and share the inner boundary of the flank, the splice site facing the candidate: the donor of the upstream flank and the acceptor of the downstream one. On "+" that is the end of the left exon and the start of the right one; on "-" the reverse. The outer boundaries may differ.

"identical"

the two exons are identical (same start and same end). The strictest setting.

inverse

If TRUE, swaps the up and down transcripts: find_se() then identifies included exons instead of skipped exons, find_cse() consecutive included exons, and find_ri() spliced introns instead of retained introns.

...

Further arguments passed to GenomicRanges::findOverlaps() when matching flanking exons, e.g. minoverlap = 5L to require at least 5 bp of overlap. Do not pass select, which changes the return type. maxgap can also be used, to let "over" and "boundary" match exons that do not overlap at all.

verbose

If TRUE, prints progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

A GRanges object with the detected exon ranges and the following additional metadata columns:

event_type

The type of splicing event detected (e.g. "se", "ie", "cse", "cie", "mxe", "ri", "si", "a5ss", "a3ss", "atss", "ates").

event_tx_id

Transcript ID of the paired transcript involved in the event.

event_estimate

DTU coefficient of the paired transcript.

event_<col>

One column per name in metadata(gr)$additional_columns, prefixed with event_, carrying the corresponding value from the paired transcript.

find_se(): skipped exons

find_ie(): included exons

find_cse(): consecutive skipped exons, i.e. runs of two or more adjacent exons skipped together, one row per exon

find_cie(): consecutive included exons

find_mxe(): mutually exclusive exons

find_ri(): retained introns

find_si(): spliced introns

find_a5ss(): alternative 5' splice sites

find_a3ss(): alternative 3' splice sites

find_atss(): alternative transcription start sites — first exons that begin transcription at a different coordinate

find_ates(): alternative transcription end sites — last exons that end transcription at a different coordinate

find_all_events(): all detected events

Examples


# make some mock data and run the function
gr <- create_mock_data(n_genes = 2, n_tx_per_gene = 4, n_exons_per_tx = 4) |>
  preprocess(coef_col = "estimate") |>
  generate_se(n_events = 1)

# this should find the skipped exon events we generated
find_se(gr, type = "boundary")
#> GRanges object with 1 range and 8 metadata columns:
#>       seqnames    ranges strand |   gene_id     tx_id exon_rank  estimate
#>          <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle> | <integer> <numeric> <integer> <numeric>
#>   [1]    chr11   101-105      + |         2         5         2 -0.687911
#>       sim_event  event_type event_tx_id event_estimate
#>       <logical> <character>   <numeric>      <numeric>
#>   [1]      TRUE          se           8        0.53935
#>   -------
#>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths

# included exons: the same edit made to a down transcript
gr_ie <- create_mock_data(
  n_genes = 2, n_tx_per_gene = 4, n_exons_per_tx = 4
) |>
  preprocess(coef_col = "estimate") |>
  generate_ie(n_events = 1)

find_ie(gr_ie, type = "boundary")
#> GRanges object with 1 range and 8 metadata columns:
#>       seqnames    ranges strand |   gene_id     tx_id exon_rank  estimate
#>          <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle> | <integer> <numeric> <integer> <numeric>
#>   [1]     chr1     11-15      + |         1         2         2  0.485274
#>       sim_event  event_type event_tx_id event_estimate
#>       <logical> <character>   <numeric>      <numeric>
#>   [1]      TRUE          ie           1      -0.980135
#>   -------
#>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths


# an up transcript skips a run of two consecutive exons
gr_cse <- create_mock_data(
  n_genes = 2, n_tx_per_gene = 4, n_exons_per_tx = 5
) |>
  preprocess(coef_col = "estimate") |>
  generate_cse(n_events = 1, n_skip = 2)

find_cse(gr_cse)

#>   [3]     chr7     21-25      + |         1         3         3 -0.9440879
#>   [4]     chr7     31-35      + |         1         3         4 -0.9440879
#>   [5]     chr7     21-25      + |         1         4         3 -0.0612314
#>   [6]     chr7     31-35      + |         1         4         4 -0.0612314
#>       sim_event  event_type event_tx_id event_estimate
#>       <logical> <character>   <numeric>      <numeric>
#>   [1]      TRUE         cse           2       0.889367
#>   [2]      TRUE         cse           2       0.889367
#>   [3]      TRUE         cse           2       0.889367
#>   [4]      TRUE         cse           2       0.889367
#>   [5]      TRUE         cse           2       0.889367
#>   [6]      TRUE         cse           2       0.889367

# find_se() only reports an exon skipped on its own, so finds nothing
find_se(gr_cse)
#> GRanges object with 0 ranges and 0 metadata columns:
#>    seqnames    ranges strand
#>       <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle>

#>   seqinfo: no sequences
